title: 星巴克，放进全球咖啡坐标系
market: 美国 / 中国 / 英国 / 加拿大 / 日本 / 澳大利亚；各品牌当地市场观察
summary: 星巴克同时强调咖啡馆体验与数字化便利。瑞幸代表以移动端为核心的高便利模式；Komeda 与 The Coffee Club 提供停留与餐饮体验的参考；Costa 和 Tim Hortons 则展示不同的咖啡、食物与会员组合。这是跨市场的模式对照，不能据此推断它们在同一城市的直接替代率、消费者偏好或经营表现。

dimensions.name: 咖啡馆体验
dimensions.rubric: 依据品牌公开表达、空间与服务描述评估：0–25 以取走为主，50 混合场景，75–100 明确强调停留。不是实际门店体验或满意度测量。

dimensions.name: 数字化便利
dimensions.rubric: 按已确认的功能评估：25 信息与找店，50 会员及支付，75 预点单取餐，100 数字化贯穿购买。分数不表示速度、用户量或应用质量。

dimensions.name: 餐食广度
dimensions.rubric: 依据菜单类别粗分：25 少量烘焙轻食，50 早餐与有限午餐，75 多种正餐与早餐，100 广泛全天餐饮。非菜品数量统计。

dimensions.name: 饮品多样性
dimensions.rubric: 按已观察的饮品类别与风味扩展评估，50 为经典咖啡加数类非咖啡，75–100 为多种冷热、风味与非咖啡选择。不推断上新速度。

dimensions.name: 居家产品延伸
dimensions.rubric: 依据居家咖啡或零售产品目录评估延伸程度；仅有电商入口时不推断完整品类。未核实留空，不能把未找到当作不存在。

sources.title: Starbucks：Back to Starbucks 时间线
sources.evidence: 官方将咖啡馆的欢迎感、交流与手工制作咖啡作为转型重点。

sources.title: Starbucks Rewards 使用条款（美国）
sources.evidence: 条款说明应用内移动点单、关联支付方式，以及到店扫码获得会员权益。

sources.title: Starbucks 美国菜单
sources.evidence: 菜单分类包括咖啡、Frappuccino、早餐、午餐及 VIA 即溶咖啡等。

sources.title: 瑞幸咖啡：关于我们
sources.evidence: 品牌描述使用移动互联网与数据的新零售模式，并强调便利与产品创新。

sources.title: 瑞幸 2025 年第一季度业绩会材料
sources.evidence: 材料记录生椰系列、饮品与轻食上新。仅用于确认产品方向，不推算当前完整菜单。

sources.title: Costa：Click & Collect
sources.evidence: 英国参与门店支持应用内选择餐饮、提前支付、到店取餐，并关联 Costa Club。

sources.title: Costa 英国菜单（搜索索引）
sources.evidence: 官方菜单的检索摘录显示咖啡、Frappé、冷饮、早餐、午餐、烘焙与零食分类；完整页面抓取受限。

sources.title: Tim Hortons：Scan & Pay
sources.evidence: 官方说明应用内一次扫码完成支付、积分获得及兑换，覆盖参与的加拿大和美国门店。

sources.title: Tim Hortons：加拿大 2025 年受欢迎产品
sources.evidence: 官方回顾提及 Double Double、Iced Capp 与 Timbits 等代表产品；不当作 2026 年偏好调查。

sources.title: Tim Hortons：早餐卷与应用取餐
sources.evidence: 官方报道加拿大早餐卷可经应用选择配送或取餐；用于确认早餐与数字功能。

sources.title: Tim Hortons：午晚餐 Wrap 组合
sources.evidence: 官方加拿大活动确认午晚餐卷饼场景；不将限时价格作为跨国价格依据。

sources.title: Komeda：放松空间的设计
sources.evidence: 官网强调宽敞座席、沙发、桌面与隔断，以提供类似客厅的放松空间。

sources.title: Komeda 日本菜单
sources.evidence: 官网列出早餐、饮品、甜品、小食、儿童菜单、商品与外带；门店菜单存在差异。

sources.title: Komeda 官方应用介绍
sources.evidence: 官方应用说明可注册 KOMECA 并在应用内出示支付；未据此确认普遍的提前点单能力。

sources.title: The Coffee Club 澳大利亚全天菜单
sources.evidence: 菜单提供早餐、三明治、沙拉与多种主食，并列出配送和 Click & Collect 入口；部分店型菜单有限。

sources.title: The Coffee Club 澳大利亚官网
sources.evidence: 官网列出咖啡及零售入口、饮品菜单、会员应用和积分权益。

sources.title: Costa 英国 Flat White
sources.evidence: 官网产品页确认 Flat White。

sources.title: The Coffee Club 饮品菜单
sources.evidence: 官方饮品菜单列出 Flat White，且注明部分店型菜单限制。

sources.title: Komeda 2025 年报告（产品方向）
sources.evidence: 官方报告提及 Shiro-Noir、抹茶饮品与合作产品；用于确认经典产品方向。

brands.name: 星巴克
brands.positioning: 咖啡馆体验与数字化购买并行。
brands.audience: 需要日常咖啡、熟悉选择与见面空间的人群。
brands.improvement: 把“高便利”与“愿意停留”分开验证：在同城门店测试取餐动线与座席体验，跟踪取餐等待、复访和堂食满意度。

experience.rationale: 咖啡馆与交流是公开表达的重点；属于定位评估。

digital.rationale: 移动点单与关联支付支持完整数字流程。

food.rationale: 早餐和午餐类别扩大了饮品以外的场景。

drinks.rationale: 咖啡与多种调制饮品类别共同构成菜单。

retail.rationale: VIA 等居家产品体现门店以外的延伸。

brands.name: 瑞幸咖啡
brands.positioning: 移动端驱动、强调便利与产品创新的咖啡模式。
brands.audience: 重视日常购买便利与风味选择的咖啡消费者。
brands.improvement: 用单城测试辨别风味新鲜感与稳定复购：比较核心款和新品的复购周期，避免仅用上新数量衡量竞争力。

experience.rationale: 公开定位强调便利新零售，未据此代表每一家门店。

digital.rationale: 移动互联网贯穿其公开描述的新零售模式。

food.rationale: 已确认轻食上新，但缺少完整当前菜单；低置信粗评。

drinks.rationale: 生椰系列与饮品创新体现风味扩展；并非上新速度排名。

retail.rationale: 未充分核实中国市场居家产品目录，留空。

brands.name: Costa Coffee
brands.positioning: 咖啡馆、餐食与应用取餐结合的日常咖啡品牌。
brands.audience: 在外带、休息与轻餐之间切换的日常消费者。
brands.improvement: 在本地测试能否形成更清晰的使用场景，例如“稳定的工作日咖啡加午餐”，用组合购买率和复访验证。

experience.rationale: 门店现制与多餐饮类别提示混合场景；空间体验证据较弱。

digital.rationale: 参与门店支持应用预订、预付和取餐。

food.rationale: 可见早餐、午餐、烘焙和零食分类。

drinks.rationale: 可见咖啡、Frappé、茶与其他冷饮分类。

retail.rationale: 本轮未核实居家产品目录，留空。

brands.name: Tim Hortons
brands.positioning: 咖啡、烘焙与多时段餐食组合的便利场景参考。
brands.audience: 需要日常咖啡、早餐和便捷餐食的人群。
brands.improvement: 测试食物扩展是否强化咖啡购买，关注食物连带率与服务复杂度；不要仅以菜单更广作为改善目标。

experience.rationale: 应用取餐和多时段餐食指向便利场景；不是空间实测。

digital.rationale: 扫码支付、会员和应用取餐覆盖多个环节。

food.rationale: 确认早餐及午晚餐 Wrap 场景。

drinks.rationale: 代表产品覆盖咖啡与冰饮；不是完整菜单计数。

retail.rationale: 本轮未核实加拿大居家产品目录，留空。

brands.name: Komeda 珈琲
brands.positioning: 以舒适停留空间和咖啡餐食为核心的参考模式。
brands.audience: 重视舒适座席、慢节奏交流与早餐的人群。
brands.improvement: 验证更便利的点单能否改善体验且不损害停留感；同时观察点单等待与堂食满意度，先从少量门店开始。

experience.rationale: 官网明确描述客厅式空间、沙发、宽敞座席和隔断。

digital.rationale: 已确认应用内支付功能；未确认普遍预点单能力。

food.rationale: 早餐、小食、儿童与甜品类别构成餐食延伸。

drinks.rationale: 可见饮品与甜品体系；未对完整品类计数。

retail.rationale: 存在商品与网店入口，但范围未充分核实。

brands.name: The Coffee Club
brands.positioning: 咖啡与全天餐饮结合的澳大利亚参考品牌。
brands.audience: 在咖啡、早午餐、见面与正餐之间切换的人群。
brands.improvement: 测试咖啡专业表达与餐饮广度的平衡；以咖啡单独复访、餐饮连带率和高峰服务时间验证。

experience.rationale: 全天餐饮组合支持停留场景，但不同店型差异明显。

digital.rationale: 官网提供 Click & Collect、配送及会员应用。

food.rationale: 完整菜单覆盖早餐、三明治、沙拉与多类主食。

drinks.rationale: 咖啡和饮品菜单并列；范围为低置信粗评。

retail.rationale: 官网存在咖啡零售入口，具体广度需进一步核查。

opportunities.title: 把“快捷”与“停留”拆成两种服务承诺
opportunities.detail: 星巴克的数字流程与咖啡馆主张同时存在。对照瑞幸和 Komeda，可检验两类场景是否在门店互相干扰。
opportunities.action: 选择同城匹配门店，试验独立取餐动线；比较取餐等待、堂食满意度、复访，先设成功门槛。

opportunities.title: 让餐食承担明确的使用场景
opportunities.detail: The Coffee Club 的全天餐饮与 Tim Hortons 的早餐、午餐场景，提示食品可以补充咖啡消费；菜单更大不必然更有竞争力。
opportunities.action: 在当地验证一个重点时段的咖啡餐食组合；观察增量毛利、连带率、浪费与服务时间，再决定是否扩展。

opportunities.title: 把“独特风味”变成可持续复购
opportunities.detail: 生椰系列与 Frappuccino 等代表产品提供辨识度参考，但公开产品资料不能说明长期需求或购买意愿。
opportunities.action: 用消费者访谈与小规模对照试验，比较核心产品和新风味的复购、偏好原因及替代对象。

limitations: 样本为六个国家的代表性模式观察，不是全球竞品穷举。国家标签表示本次观察市场，不能用来判断所有海外门店。
分数由研究者按公开资料粗评，非品牌官方评分、消费者感知调查、市场份额或财务竞争力。5–10 分差距不应解读为精确差距。
各市场的价格、收入与产品版本不同，本样本不比较绝对售价。跨国借鉴方向需在同市场、同规格、同时间重新验证。
部分依据是历史产品材料或官方搜索摘录。它们确认模式与产品方向，不能证明当前每家门店或完整菜单一致。未知的居家产品范围已留空。
优势、目标人群和改善方向属于研究推断；改善动作需要实验验证。图上邻近或空白，不等同于直接竞争或存在需求。
拖动、改名和自定义维度属于手动情景。矩阵保留原值依据，分析页不会被坐标编辑自动改写。

en.title: Starbucks in the global coffee landscape
en.market: US / China / UK / Canada / Japan / Australia; each brand observed in its local market
en.summary: Starbucks combines a café experience with digital convenience. Luckin provides an app-centric reference, while Komeda and The Coffee Club offer contrasts in dwell time and dining. Costa and Tim Hortons illustrate different coffee, food and loyalty combinations. These are cross-market business-model references, not evidence of local substitution, consumer preference or financial performance.

dimensions.name: Café experience
dimensions.rubric: Assess stated formats and service propositions: 0–25 pickup-led, 50 mixed occasions, 75–100 explicit emphasis on dwelling. Not a measured store-experience or satisfaction score.

dimensions.name: Digital convenience
dimensions.rubric: Assess documented functions: 25 information/store finder, 50 loyalty and payment, 75 order-ahead collection, 100 digital purchasing throughout. Scores do not measure speed, adoption or app quality.

dimensions.name: Food range
dimensions.rubric: Coarse menu-based assessment: 25 light bakery/snacks, 50 breakfast and limited lunch, 75 several meal occasions, 100 broad all-day dining. Not an exact item count.

dimensions.name: Beverage range
dimensions.rubric: Assess observed categories and flavor extensions: 50 classics plus some non-coffee categories; 75–100 multiple hot/cold, flavored and non-coffee choices. Not a launch-rate measure.

dimensions.name: At-home extension
dimensions.rubric: Assess verified at-home coffee or retail ranges. A store link alone does not establish breadth. Leave unverified ranges null; absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.

sources.title: Starbucks: Back to Starbucks timeline
sources.evidence: The official timeline emphasizes welcoming coffeehouses, connection and handcrafted coffee.

sources.title: Starbucks Rewards terms (US)
sources.evidence: The terms describe mobile orders, linked payment methods and in-store member scanning.

sources.title: Starbucks US menu
sources.evidence: The menu includes coffee, Frappuccino, breakfast, lunch and VIA instant coffee.

sources.title: Luckin Coffee: About us
sources.evidence: The brand describes a mobile-internet and data-based retail model, convenience and product innovation.

sources.title: Luckin Q1 2025 earnings-call material
sources.evidence: The material discusses coconut products, beverage and light-food launches. It confirms product directions, not a current full menu.

sources.title: Costa: Click & Collect
sources.evidence: Participating UK stores support app-based food/drink orders, advance payment, collection and Costa Club.

sources.title: Costa UK menu (search index)
sources.evidence: Official search extracts show coffee, frappé, cold drinks, breakfast, lunch, bakery and snacks; full-page retrieval was limited.

sources.title: Tim Hortons: Scan & Pay
sources.evidence: The official page describes one-scan payment, earning and redemption at participating Canadian and US restaurants.

sources.title: Tim Hortons: Canada’s 2025 favorite menu items
sources.evidence: The retrospective identifies Double Double, Iced Capp and Timbits; it is not treated as a 2026 preference survey.

sources.title: Tim Hortons: Breakfast wraps and app pickup
sources.evidence: The official article describes Canadian breakfast wraps and delivery/pickup through the app.

sources.title: Tim Hortons: Lunch and dinner wrap offer
sources.evidence: The Canadian promotion confirms lunch/dinner wrap occasions; its limited-time price is not used for cross-country price comparisons.

sources.title: Komeda: Designing a place to relax
sources.evidence: The official page describes spacious seating, sofas, tables and partitions for a living-room-like setting.

sources.title: Komeda Japan menu
sources.evidence: The official menu lists morning sets, drinks, desserts, snacks, kids, retail and takeaway, with store variation.

sources.title: Komeda official app listing
sources.evidence: The official app listing describes registering KOMECA for payment; it does not establish general order-ahead capability.

sources.title: The Coffee Club Australia all-day menu
sources.evidence: The menu covers breakfast, sandwiches, salads and meals, with delivery and Click & Collect links; some formats have limited menus.

sources.title: The Coffee Club Australia official site
sources.evidence: The site lists coffee retail, drinks menus, a loyalty app and points benefits.

sources.title: Costa UK Flat White
sources.evidence: The official product page confirms Flat White.

sources.title: The Coffee Club drinks menu
sources.evidence: The official drinks menu lists Flat White and notes format-specific limitations.

sources.title: Komeda 2025 report (product direction)
sources.evidence: The official report features Shiro-Noir, matcha drinks and collaborations as product directions.

brands.name: Starbucks
brands.positioning: A café experience paired with digital purchasing.
brands.audience: People seeking daily coffee, familiar choices and a meeting place.
brands.improvement: Test convenience and dwell experience separately in one city: measure pickup wait, repeat visits and dine-in satisfaction.

experience.rationale: Coffeehouse connection is an explicit proposition; this is a positioning assessment.

digital.rationale: Mobile orders and linked payments support a substantial digital journey.

food.rationale: Breakfast and lunch extend the offer beyond beverages.

drinks.rationale: Coffee and multiple prepared-beverage categories feature in the menu.

retail.rationale: VIA and related at-home products extend the brand beyond cafés.

brands.name: Luckin Coffee
brands.positioning: A mobile-led coffee proposition emphasizing convenience and product innovation.
brands.audience: Coffee buyers seeking everyday convenience and flavor variety.
brands.improvement: Use a single-city test to distinguish novelty from retention: compare repeat-purchase cycles for core and new products.

experience.rationale: The stated model emphasizes convenient retail, not every individual store format.

digital.rationale: Mobile technology is central to the stated retail model.

food.rationale: Light-food launches are confirmed; the current full menu is not. Low-confidence estimate.

drinks.rationale: Coconut products and beverage launches indicate flavor breadth, not a launch-rate ranking.

retail.rationale: The at-home range in China was not sufficiently verified.

brands.name: Costa Coffee
brands.positioning: An everyday coffee proposition combining cafés, food and app collection.
brands.audience: Everyday customers moving between takeaway, breaks and light meals.
brands.improvement: Test a sharper local occasion, such as a dependable weekday coffee-and-lunch routine, using basket attachment and repeat visits.

experience.rationale: In-store preparation and food categories suggest mixed occasions; spatial-experience evidence is limited.

digital.rationale: Participating stores offer app preordering, payment and collection.

food.rationale: Visible categories include breakfast, lunch, bakery and snacks.

drinks.rationale: Visible categories include coffee, frappé, tea and other cold drinks.

retail.rationale: The at-home range was not verified in this research pass.

brands.name: Tim Hortons
brands.positioning: A convenient coffee, bakery and meal-occasion reference.
brands.audience: People seeking routine coffee, breakfast and convenient meals.
brands.improvement: Test whether food expansion reinforces coffee occasions; track attachment and operational complexity rather than maximizing menu breadth.

experience.rationale: App pickup and meal occasions indicate convenience; store ambience was not measured.

digital.rationale: Scan-to-pay, loyalty and app pickup cover multiple purchase stages.

food.rationale: Breakfast plus lunch/dinner wrap occasions are confirmed.

drinks.rationale: Signature products span coffee and iced drinks; not a full menu count.

retail.rationale: The Canadian at-home range was not verified in this pass.

brands.name: Komeda Coffee
brands.positioning: A reference model centered on comfortable dwell spaces, coffee and food.
brands.audience: People valuing comfortable seating, relaxed conversation and breakfast.
brands.improvement: Test whether easier ordering improves convenience without weakening the relaxed experience, tracking waits and dine-in satisfaction in a few stores.

experience.rationale: The site explicitly describes living-room-like space, sofas, spacious seating and partitions.

digital.rationale: App payment is documented; broad order-ahead capability is not confirmed.

food.rationale: Morning, snack, kids and dessert categories extend meal occasions.

drinks.rationale: Drinks and dessert categories are visible; full categories were not counted.

retail.rationale: Retail and shop links exist, but range breadth was not sufficiently verified.

brands.name: The Coffee Club
brands.positioning: An Australian reference combining coffee with all-day dining.
brands.audience: People combining coffee, brunch, meetups and meals.
brands.improvement: Test the balance between coffee identity and dining breadth using coffee-only repeat visits, food attachment and peak service time.

experience.rationale: All-day dining supports dwell occasions, with substantial format differences.

digital.rationale: The site offers Click & Collect, delivery and a loyalty app.

food.rationale: The full menu covers breakfast, sandwiches, salads and several meal types.

drinks.rationale: Coffee and drinks menus are listed; range is a low-confidence estimate.

retail.rationale: A coffee retail section is visible; its full breadth requires further verification.

opportunities.title: Separate quick pickup from dwell experience
opportunities.detail: Starbucks combines digital journeys with a coffeehouse proposition. Luckin and Komeda provide references for testing whether the two occasions interfere in stores.
opportunities.action: Test separate pickup flows in matched stores within one city. Predefine success thresholds for wait, dine-in satisfaction and repeat visits.

opportunities.title: Give food a clear occasion
opportunities.detail: The Coffee Club’s all-day menu and Tim Hortons’ breakfast/lunch occasions suggest complementary uses for food. A larger menu is not necessarily more competitive.
opportunities.action: Test a coffee-and-food combination in one local daypart. Track incremental margin, attachment, waste and service time before expanding.

opportunities.title: Turn distinctive flavors into repeat occasions
opportunities.detail: Coconut products and Frappuccino offer distinctiveness references, but product descriptions do not prove sustained demand or willingness to buy.
opportunities.action: Use interviews and a small controlled trial to compare core products and new flavors on repeat purchase, preference drivers and alternatives.

limitations: This is a six-country set of representative models, not an exhaustive global competitor census. Country labels indicate observed markets, not all overseas stores.
Scores are coarse analyst assessments, not brand-reported ratings, perception research, market share or financial competitiveness. Small differences are not precise gaps.
Prices, incomes and products differ across markets. This sample does not compare absolute prices. Validate transfers in the same market, specification and period.
Some evidence comes from historical material or official search extracts. It supports directions, not uniform current stores or full menus. Unverified at-home ranges remain null.
Strengths, audiences and improvements are analyst inferences requiring validation. Proximity or empty space on the map is not proof of rivalry or demand.
Dragging, relabeling and custom dimensions are manual scenarios. Original score evidence remains; narrative analysis is not rewritten by coordinate edits.
